title: test(ai): cover the two fixes that shipped in v6.4.2 without tests
body:
These 22 tests were written alongside the fixes but left out of the v6.4.2 release: that branch was cut off main, and main has no `test` script and no vitest dependency, so the files would have sat there unrunnable. staging has vitest, so they land here.

They lock the two things neither build nor lint can see, and both are the exact drift that caused the original bugs:

  • the chat attachment guide has to tell the model the file IS the
    subject, and has to order the answer BEFORE any follow-up question.
    Reversing those two lines is what made an attached photo produce an
    interrogation about the photo instead of a description of it.
  • the vision mime allowlist has to reject HEIC. The community path
    filtered correctly while the chat path accepted any `image/*`, so an
    iPhone library photo reached Gemini, came back 400, and surfaced to
    the user as "שירות ה-AI לא זמין" with nothing pointing at the file
    format.

The aiExtract tests also pin the non-obvious shape of a FunctionsHttpError: invoke() nulls `data` and hides the response body in error.context, so a plain `if (error) return error.message` silently converts a deliberate "scan disabled" into "we could not read your document".

Verified against staging at 81f71fe, which matters: b61edc7 added advisor-call counting to ai-proxy, the module these tests import from. Suite is 303 passing across 22 files, eslint 0 errors, no production file touched.

All three fixes these tests cover were confirmed on a real device today via a debug APK built from the v6.4.2 tag.

title: ci: deploy an Edge Function from the browser, and leave a record
body:
Every one of the 17 Edge Functions has been deployed by hand from a developer machine, and nothing recorded which one shipped, from which commit, or when. That is the same blind spot the SQL ledger exists to close, and it bit us today: the scan kill switch was merged into main, reviewed, released as v6.4.2 and tagged, and is still completely inert in production, because deploying a function is a separate manual act that no process covered. Code in main is not code that is running.

Dispatching from Actions puts the function, the ref, the SHA and the commit subject into the run summary, so the Actions history becomes the deploy ledger. It also means a deploy no longer needs a terminal.

The part worth reading: the JWT cross-check
--------------------------------------------
A naive "deploy the function you picked" workflow is actively dangerous here, because 12 of the 17 functions are deliberately PUBLIC and the correct flag is per-function:

  • unsubscribe    reached from an email link, security is an HMAC token.
                   Deploy it with verification ON and every opt-out link
                   in every email we send stops working. That is a
                   compliance failure, not a bug.
  • overpass-proxy FindGarage works for guests, who have no JWT at all.
  • the 10 dispatch/cron functions, called by pg_cron and webhooks.

None of those failures surfaces anywhere near the deploy that caused them, which is exactly why this cannot be left to whoever fills in the form. So the function's own source is the authority: the check reads its header and refuses to run if the request contradicts it.

The pattern accepts the several ways they phrase it, because they are not consistent — ":" in some, "=" in others, "--no-verify-jwt" in others. My first attempt only matched the colon form and classified `unsubscribe` as needing verification, which is precisely the mistake that would have broken the unsubscribe links. Caught by running the classifier over all 17 before committing.

Three functions are on a verified-ON list because I read their actual auth gate rather than inferring from silence: ai-proxy (401 "Missing bearer token" + auth.getUser), send-email (401 "missing authorization" + auth.getUser), admin-impersonate (requires the caller's own JWT to satisfy is_admin).

Anything else FAILS CLOSED. Silence is not evidence that a function wants verification: dispatch-admin-alert gates on an x-dispatch-secret header and is called server-to-server, so a default-ON deploy could reject its callers before it even runs. It is blocked until someone works out its stance and records it. A blocked deploy costs minutes; a wrong one costs a silent outage nobody connects to this.

Setup, once: add SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. NOTE it is account-scoped, not project-scoped — whoever holds it reaches every Supabase project on the account.

The project ref is hardcoded on purpose and is not a secret: it is the host of VITE_SUPABASE_URL, which Vite inlines into the public browser bundle, so it is already readable by anyone who loads the app.

Verified: YAML parses, all five run: blocks pass `bash -n`, and the classifier was run against all 17 functions on main (12 OFF declared in source, 3 ON verified, 1 blocked). CI-only change, so no version bump.

title: release: v6.4.0 — view-as impersonation, invite delivery, Gate-3 fixes
body:
## v6.4.0 — admin view-as impersonation, invite delivery, RLS fix

22 commits. Promotes the work held out of v6.3.0 ("view-as held") to production.

### What ships
- **Admin view-as → real impersonation.** Sessions identify a **(user, account)** pair; a short-lived JWT makes `auth.uid()` the target, so every RLS policy and RPC behaves as it does for the real user. Replaces the previous `is_viewing()` allowlist model.
- **Business invite delivery** for already-registered invitees (email + surfaced banner + accept/decline during view-as).
- **RLS write-leak fix** — active membership now required for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on 6 tables (pending members could write).
- **Admin ownership reassignment**, including a deliberately ownerless state.

### Gate-3 review findings — all fixed and adversarially re-verified
1. `admin-impersonate` Gate 3 made **fail-closed** (was fail-open on any `is_admin` error).
2. **View-as token race** — the forbidden state (viewAs null with an impersonation token installed) proven unreachable across all interleavings over three verification rounds (generation guard + install-time invariant + exit second-clear).
3. **Second vehicle localStorage cache** no longer persists a viewed customer's data on the admin's device.
4. `stamp_acting_admin` preserves attribution on a normal UPDATE.
5. Pending-invite banner clears after accept/decline during view-as.

### Gates
All 7 in-session production gates passed. CI (build, lint, query-timeout, view-as-identity) runs on this PR.

### ⚠️ Two manual steps AFTER merge (not performed by the merge)
1. **Deploy the edge function:** `supabase functions deploy admin-impersonate` — the fail-closed fix lives only in the TS until deployed.
2. **Re-apply** `supabase-impersonation-attribution-2026-07-24.sql` (idempotent) — the corrected trigger; the shared prod DB still has the old one.

### Not included
Concurrent vehicle-cap feature (still in progress in the tree) and the gates-upgrade initiative (separate follow-up PR).

title: fix(ios): wire CapacitorCommunityAppleSignIn pod + static import
body:
**HOTFIX for the stuck Apple Sign-In button.** TestFlight build 158 had the button visible but tapping did nothing.

Two root causes:

1. `ios/App/Podfile` was missing `pod 'CapacitorCommunityAppleSignIn'`. `npx cap sync ios` updates Package.swift (SPM) but the iOS build uses CocoaPods. Native bridge had no handler → JS call hung forever.
2. `src/pages/AuthPage.jsx` used dynamic `await import()` with `@vite-ignore`. WKWebView has no module resolver for bare specifiers, so the import itself hung. Switched to static top-of-file import.

After merge → re-trigger ios-release.yml → new TestFlight build → native Apple sheet should appear.
